## Paper

The Economics of Matching: Stability and Incentives

## World

labor_market

## Institution

Deferred acceptance with incentive constraints.

## Agent type

Workers/students and employers/colleges with strategic reports.

## Theoretical benchmark

Deferred acceptance is strategy-proof for the proposing side under standard assumptions but not for both sides.

## Learning setup

Agents learn or choose reported preferences under a fixed matching protocol.

## Metrics

Truthful-report rate, manipulation gain, stability, welfare, side-specific profitable deviations.

## Main result

No stable matching procedure exists which gives all players an incentive to reveal their preferences; however, procedures exist which give one side the incentive to reveal true preferences.

## What they prove

Theorem 3: No stable matching procedure for the general matching problem exists for which truthful revelation of preferences is a dominant strategy for all agents.

## What they only simulate

The simulation of stable outcomes and preference profiles under different institutional arrangements.

## What they do NOT test

The paper does not test the robustness of the results under different preference structures or institutional variations.

## What we need to reproduce

Do not interpret worker-side misreport profits under worker-proposing DA as expected theory; test side-specific incentives.

## How our project differs

The paper establishes incentive limits of stable matching. The repo currently has learning workers and fixed employer preferences, so incentive claims are side-specific.

## Implementation obligations

State proposing side; enumerate fixed benchmark deviations; manipulation-gain diagnostics; do not claim two-sided strategy-proofness.

## Metrics to compare in our repo

labor_market_benchmark_cases.json; manipulation-gain diagnostics; outputs/labor_market_full.

## Failure modes to audit

Calling any non-truthful report manipulation without profitable deviation; testing only the strategy-proof side; no fixed preference hand cases.

## Project code comparison

Compare The Economics of Matching: Stability and Incentives to Labor Market benchmark cases. The repo should use Roth to avoid false manipulation claims under worker-proposing DA.
